summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain that worsened with eating and was associated with chest pressure and shortness of breath. Evaluation ruled out cardiac ischemia with normal EKGs and negative troponins, and CT angiography showed no pulmonary embolism, aortic syndrome, or mesenteric ischemia. The abdominal pain improved with sucralfate and acid suppression. Black stools were attributed to iron supplementation, and no active bleeding was found. The patient was discharged home with stable symptoms, continuation of cardiac and diabetes medications, new prescriptions for sucralfate and simethicone, and follow-up planned with gastroenterology for further evaluation of chronic abdominal pain.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
